Network Trauma Research series: Modeling Trauma Complexity: Rodent Platforms for Studying Bone Healing and Hemorrhagic Shock.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions often accompanied by physiological instability, remains a major global health burden with high morbidity and mortality. Among the most clinically relevant two-injury combinations, long-bone fractures and hemorrhagic shock are particularly important, as both critically influence systemic inflammation, remote organ dysfunction such as lung or kidney damage, and tissue regeneration itself. To improve translational understanding of these complex interactions, robust small-animal models, particularly murine systems, have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying fracture healing, hypovolemic shock, and their combined effects. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current rodent models for isolated fracture, hemorrhagic shock, and combination trauma. Key methodological variables, such as fracture induction methods, fixation strategies, hemorrhage protocols, anesthesia and analgesia, and the influence of age, sex, and comorbidities are outlined to support informed model selection. Additionally, this manuscript highlights the challenges and opportunities in designing clinically relevant "double-hit" models that mimic real-world trauma patterns while maintaining high reproducibility and animal welfare standards. Collectively, the summarized evidence underscores the importance of standardized, physiologically meaningful preclinical trauma models to advance mechanistic insights and foster the development of effective therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Dynamic phenotyping and organ cross-talk in sepsis-associated organ injury: from physiological trajectories to precision critical care.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated organ injury remains a major cause of mortality in critically ill patients. Conventional assessment relies largely on physiological indicators, including lactate, mean arterial pressure (MAP), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, creatinine, urine output, and organ dysfunction scores. However, these isolated values or single-variable trends may incompletely capture the temporal instability and biological heterogeneity that characterize sepsis. Increasing evidence indicates that dynamic trajectories, variability patterns, and evolving subphenotypes may better characterize disease progression, organ recovery, and treatment responsiveness. In parallel, critical care medicine is moving from syndrome-level classification toward treatable traits, individualized treatment effects, and precision critical care. Dynamic phenotyping focuses on physiological trajectories, including lactate clearance, oxygenation evolution, hemodynamic variability, glycemic variability, and renal recovery, but its major value may lie in interpreting relationships among trajectories across organ systems. Interpretation of dynamic phenotypes therefore requires attention to cross-system temporal relationships, including coordinated recovery, coupled deterioration, and discordant recovery. From this trajectory-based perspective, sepsis-associated organ injury can be viewed as an interconnected multiorgan network involving lung-kidney, gut-lung, gut-liver, gut-kidney, and endothelial-organ cross-talk. Organ cross-talk may help explain dynamic coupling among organ systems, whereas microcirculatory-mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to trajectory mismatch through impaired tissue perfusion, oxygen delivery-utilization uncoupling, bioenergetic failure, maladaptive metabolic reprogramming, and defective mitochondrial quality control. This trajectory-based perspective may inform future precision critical care, while most trajectory-guided strategies remain investigational and require prospective validation before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Burn Care in Prisons: Ethical Dilemmas in Correctional Health Care.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn injuries among incarcerated individuals represent an underexplored intersection of medical ethics, correctional policy, and health equity. Although scholarship increasingly examines vulnerable groups such as refugees and undocumented patients, incarcerated patients with burn injuries remain largely absent. Dual loyalty-balancing duty to the patient with obligations to the institution or state-creates distinctive challenges that are intensified in burn care, where timely intervention, pain control, rehabilitation, and psychosocial support are critical but often constrained by security protocols and systemic neglect. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus to identify peer-reviewed articles, position statements, and ethical analyses addressing incarcerated healthcare, dual loyalty, and burn treatment (English-language, 2000-2025). A thematic synthesis identified recurring ethical tensions, clinical barriers, and potential frameworks for resolution. Findings highlight a major gap in both literature and professional discourse. Recurrent themes included restricted access to specialized burn centers, compromised informed consent under custodial oversight, inadequate rehabilitative services, and disproportionate suffering linked to institutional neglect. Dual loyalty emerges as a central driver of ethical conflict, often pitting patient dignity against correctional authority. Elevating incarcerated burn care within burn scholarship and advocacy is necessary to uphold standards of care. Explicit attention to dual loyalty can support reforms that preserve patient dignity while maintaining institutional safety, improve outcomes, and reaffirm professional ethical commitments.

articles.title: MicroRNA-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles for Burn Wound Repair: Burn-Specific Design and Translational Perspectives.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing remains a major clinical challenge. This review evaluates microRNA-engineered extracellular vesicles as cell-free therapeutics and proposes a burn-oriented framework linking engineering strategies with burn-specific biological and clinical barriers. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Google Scholar, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure for studies published between January 1, 2021, and July 4, 2026. Burn-focused and broader wound-healing evidence was reviewed, with relevant earlier seminal studies included when necessary. Upstream parental-cell programming, downstream vesicle modification, and biomaterial-assisted delivery may improve cargo control, targeting, retention, and therapeutic performance. However, much of the available evidence remains derived from non-burn wound models. Burn-specific translation must also address burn depth, eschar, infection, hypoxia, systemic inflammation, inhalation injury, grafting requirements, dose scaling for large burns, repeat application, storage, sterility, and compatibility with debridement and grafting. MicroRNA-engineered extracellular vesicles are a versatile platform for burn wound repair, but clinical translation remains speculative without robust large-animal, infected-burn, grafting, long-term scar, and human safety data.

articles.title: Ethical Challenges of Bioprinted and Lab-Grown Skin Substitutes in Burn Care.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Severe burns continue to impose significant global morbidity and mortality, particularly where surgical and critical-care resources are limited. As survival has improved, attention has shifted toward optimizing reconstruction. Bioprinted and lab-grown skin substitutes-building on advances in tissue engineering, cellular scaffolds, and 3D bioprinting-offer new possibilities for coverage, yet raise ethical, legal, and distributive challenges that remain underexamined in burn care. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (2010-2025), supplemented by foundational legal and bioethics literature. Sources were selected for conceptual and policy relevance to ownership, consent, commercialization, intellectual property (IP), and equity in regenerative skin technologies. Fifty publications spanning burn surgery, biobanking, organoid governance, IP law, and global health were synthesized inductively. Five major ethical domains emerged: (1) ambiguous ownership and ontological status of hybrid bioprinted tissues; (2) inadequacy of consent processes to address commercialization and downstream uses of patient-derived cells; (3) complex IP environments that may restrict access and clinical innovation; (4) distributive injustice driven by high costs and global resource disparities; and (5) a near absence of empirical ethics research involving burn patients or care teams. Bioprinted and lab-grown skin substitutes could transform burn reconstruction, but current ethical and regulatory frameworks lag behind. Addressing ownership, consent, commercialization, and equity-supported by robust empirical engagement with patients-is essential for responsible integration of these technologies into burn care.

Global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases among adolescents and young adults from 1990 to 2021, with global projections to 2035.
articles.abstract: This study estimated the global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among adolescents and young adults aged 10-24 years during 1990-2021. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percentage changes, and Spearman's rank correlation evaluated associations between age-standardized rates and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI). Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models were applied to project global age-standardized rates of mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) through 2035. In 2021, NCDs accounted for approximately 404.87 thousand deaths, 129.49 million DALYs, and 100.62 million YLDs in this population. Neoplasms and cardiovascular diseases were the leading causes of NCD-related death, whereas mental disorders were the predominant source of non-fatal burden. Mortality declined in both absolute numbers and age-standardized rates during 1990-2021, whereas absolute DALYs and YLDs increased despite modest reductions or stability in age-standardized rates. Age-standardized DALY and YLD rates were higher in females, but mortality rates were higher in males. In 2021, age-standardized mortality rates were strongly negatively correlated with SDI at the country level (ρ =- 0.80, P < 0.001), whereas YLD rates showed a moderate positive correlation (ρ = 0.56, P < 0.001). ARIMA projections indicated continued declines in mortality through 2035, with DALY rates remaining stable and YLD rates declining modestly toward pre-pandemic levels. Conclusion: Despite mortality reductions, non-fatal NCD burden driven by mental disorders continues to rise. Marked disparities persist by sex and SDI levels, with high-SDI regions facing escalating disability burden and low-SDI regions confronting elevated mortality. Targeted interventions are urgently needed to advance Sustainable Development Goal Target 3.4.

articles.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Resuscitation in Pediatric Patients: A San Antonio Cohort Descriptive.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study is to describe the demographic, clinical, and prehospital care characteristics of pediatric patients receiving whole blood (WB) resuscitation by San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD). We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study to evaluate pediatric patients who received prehospital low-titer group O positive WB transfusion through the SAFD prehospital blood program between October 2018 and June 2025. The objective was to characterize patient demographics, injury patterns, resuscitative interventions, shock physiology, and outcomes among pediatric recipients in a mature civilian emergency medical services WB program. Of 1703 WB transfusions, 73 (4.3%) were pediatric. Most patients were male (76%), age range 1-17 years old with a mode of 17 years, adolescents represented 78%. Trauma accounted for 96% of cases, firearm injury (74%); all penetrating (84%), blunt (12%), with the remainder classified as medical/unknown. Vascular access was intravenous (73%), intraosseous (26%). Tranexamic acid was co-administered in 39%; 12% received ceftriaxone. When analyzed using age-adjusted Shock Index Pediatric Age-Adjusted (SIPA) thresholds (>1.2 for 1-6 years, >1.0 for 7-12 years, and >0.9 for 13-17 years), based on the initial available prehospital heart rate and systolic blood pressure, 45% of patients had an elevated SIPA, 22% had a normal SIPA, 20% were pulseless and therefore could not undergo SIPA calculation, and 14% lacked sufficient vital-sign data for classification. Survival was 50%; died 39%, and unknown outcomes 11%. Mean delta shock index values were most negative in toddlers (1-4 years) -0.97 ± 1.29, followed by children (5-11 years) -0.76 ± 1.07 and adolescents (12-17 years) -0.16 ± 0.46, indicating a greater physiologic response to resuscitation among younger pediatric patients. Pediatric WB recipients were predominantly adolescent males who sustained penetrating trauma and presented with moderate-to-severe shock. Younger age groups had larger descriptive decreases in shock index during the prehospital encounter; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup sizes and observational design.

articles.title: Hospital cost structures and resource utilisation across representative treatment pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care: a nationwide DRG-based analysis in Germany.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Implant-associated orthopaedic infections require prolonged inpatient treatment, repeated surgery and multidisciplinary care, yet nationwide evidence on how hospital resources are distributed across clinically distinct treatment pathways is limited. This study characterised hospital-side case costs, resource utilisation and aggregate expenditure across representative German diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Publicly available 2024 data from the German Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System (InEK) were analysed. Twelve representative DRGs were selected a priori from official definitions and diagnostic/procedural profiles and grouped into six treatment pathways. The InEK cost matrix reflects standardised hospital-side resource costs from participating calculation hospitals and does not represent actual DRG reimbursement. National case frequencies, length of stay and mean case costs were analysed using frequency-weighted pathway estimates, while pathway-level cost composition was calculated from aggregate component expenditure. The included DRGs represented 36,212 hospitalisations and €305.2 million in aggregate annual hospital-side expenditure represented by the selected DRGs. Mean hospital-side costs ranged from €5,859 to €22,495 per case. Ward care accounted for approximately 34-69% of pathway expenditure; operating theatre services contributed up to 39% in revision arthroplasty. Geriatric rehabilitation generated the largest aggregate expenditure (€119.0 million; 39.0%) because of high case volume, whereas complex vacuum-assisted wound care had the highest per-case cost but only 2.9% of aggregate expenditure. At the aggregated DRG level, mean length of stay was associated with mean case cost (Pearson r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.60-0.96; P < 0.001); leave-one-out correlations ranged from r = 0.79 to r = 0.96. Resource requirements differ markedly across representative DRG pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Because the selected DRGs are not infection-exclusive, the reported expenditure should not be interpreted as the national economic burden of implant-associated orthopaedic infection. The findings may inform hospital resource planning and future cost-revenue analyses.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied. The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results. Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included. Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results. The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria. Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89). Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: The "New" Frozen Frontier of World War II: Air War at Extreme Altitude.
articles.abstract: Cold injury was a largely overlooked medical and operational crisis in Allied aviation medicine in the early days of World War II. Although extreme cold had shaped military outcomes for centuries, the rapid ascent of fighting aircraft of this era to altitudes above 8000 m exposed aircrews to unprecedented hypobaric and thermal stress. Early in the conflict, aviation medicine lagged behind engineering advances, and frostbite reached epidemic proportions. The historical record reveals that inadequate equipment, poor training, flawed oxygen-delivery systems, and structural vulnerabilities of aircraft were primary contributors to injury. Moreover, awareness of the mechanisms of cold injury in the early 1940s, at least in the English-speaking world, was at such a basic level that the therapeutic paradigm of rapid rewarming of frostbite injury was not to be readily accepted until the following decade. Nonetheless, the findings of military medical investigators combined with political pressure from civilian consultants prompted high-level review of cold injury in aviators. This ultimately forced reforms at Wright Field, the center of US aeromedical development during the war. Solutions were implemented that included improved oxygen-mask design, protective plexiglass gun-port coverings, individualized cold-weather gear, and mandatory oxygen-use protocols. By mid-1944, frostbite incidence had markedly declined among aircrews. However, the failure to transfer these lessons to ground forces during the winter of 1944 to 1945 underscored persistent gaps in institutional learning and highlighted the need for systematic dissemination of operational medical knowledge across military branches.

articles.abstract: Cancer survivors have an elevated risk for developing heart failure due to prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and other overlapping co-morbid conditions. With the advancement in cancer treatment, there is an increasing number of survivors who are at an even higher risk of developing heart failure. There is a growing need for heart failure specific risk prediction models in this population to facilitate early diagnosis and timely management. This review aims to summarize most recent findings on heart failure risk prediction among patients with history of cancer. Current risk prediction models focus on heart failure risk at the time of cancer treatment and shortly thereafter. There is limited data on heart failure risk among long term survivors.

articles.title: Adaptive Workforce Strategies in Public Health Emergencies: A Quasi-Experimental Study with a Historical Control Group.
articles.abstract: Crisis-driven health care shortages require adaptive regulatory changes. Allowing advanced nursing students to provide clinical care could bolster surge capacity while enhancing professional competence. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of crisis period clinical work on nursing students' academic and licensure outcomes. A quasi-experimental study with a historical control group was conducted among 68 students enrolled in an academic career retraining track (an intensive first-entry nursing program for individuals holding a non-nursing bachelor's degree with no prior nursing background). During a major public health emergency (the COVID-19 pandemic), a work experience group (n = 23) received temporary clinical permissions before licensure, while a control group (n = 45) followed the standard curriculum without early clinical employment. Outcomes included final program grades and scores on the Governmental Licensing Examination in Nursing (GLEIN). The work experience group demonstrated significantly higher mean final grades [79.92 (SD = 5.14) versus 76.9 (SD = 9.72); difference, 3.02 (95% CI, 0.28-5.76); P =.033] and higher GLEIN scores [81.85 (SD = 6.69) versus 73.9 (SD = 9.49); difference, 7.95 (95% CI, 0.70-15.20); P =.029] compared to the control group. Regression analysis identified crisis period clinical work experience as a significant predictor of higher licensing exam performance. Temporary clinical employment of advanced nursing students during a crisis was positively associated with academic performance and higher licensing examination scores. Adaptive regulatory policies can support student academic readiness and licensure success during public health emergencies.

To cradle or not: assessing the use of a lumbar puncture cradle on lumbar puncture success rates.
articles.abstract: Neonatal and infant lumbar puncture success rates range from 50 to 80%, while traumatic lumbar punctures are reported in 30-50%. A novel lumbar puncture cradle, SMöLTAP®, designed to standardize seated positioning may improve procedural outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the first-pass success and traumatic lumbar puncture rates using the cradle compared to the lateral decubitus. This was a single-center cohort study from August 2020-October 2024 in a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Term and corrected preterm infants (≥ 37 weeks, ≤ 3 months) requiring a lumbar puncture were identified through an EPIC report. Unstable infants, those requiring opening pressure, performed under sedation or using ultrasound guidance, and charts with missing documentation were excluded. Lumbar punctures using the cradle were identified first, and a stratified random sampling technique was used to select the non-exposed cohort, in which lumbar punctures were performed in the lateral decubitus position. Chi-square analysis and logistic regression were used to analyze lumbar puncture success rates. 142 infants were included (mean age 26 days, 57% male). Cradle use was associated with a higher first-pass success rate: 63%, as opposed to 41% in the control lateral decubitus group p = 0.01. It remained significantly associated with first-pass success after a multivariable logistic regression (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.06-4.68, p = 0.03). Cradle use was associated with fewer traumatic lumbar punctures, 36% versus 59% (p = 0.01), percent difference 23% (95% CI 6.6-37.8). There was no difference in the overall success rate, 80% versus 70%, p = 0.17. The cradle is a promising tool that may improve first-pass success, reduce traumatic lumbar punctures, and provide more precise management of febrile infants requiring a lumbar puncture, thereby reducing clinical diagnostic and management challenges.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study of the Efficacy of Regional Anesthesia in Reducing Donor Site Harvest Pain in Burn Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Despite advances in burn care, the pain of burn treatment remains unresolved. The creation of donor harvest sites is often unavoidable, and the subsequent pain is difficult to treat. Regional anesthesia for the donor harvest sites can provide effective analgesia, however, there is limited literature regarding its efficacy. The purpose of this study was to assess the use of regional anesthesia for donor harvest site pain. Patients admitted to the burn center from January 1, 2011, to May 15, 2025, with thigh donor site harvest(s) were reviewed for study inclusion. Data collected included demographics, burn variables, hospital course data, and regional anesthesia procedure details. Descriptive statistics were used to determine differences between the block and non-block groups. Of the 524 patients included, 164 (31.3%) had donor site blocks and 360 (68.7%) did not. There were 77 (47%) with single shot blocks and 87 (53%) had indwelling catheters (groin or epidural). The groups were well-matched in their demographics, burn injury data, and hospital variables. The overall oral morphine equivalents (OME) and pain report levels were similar between the block and control groups in all three post-operative periods. However, causal conclusions are limited by this retrospective, heterogenous study. An appropriately protocolized prospective study is planned.

A bedside score using arrival data to identify major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring fracture: Development and validation.
articles.abstract: Early recognition of major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring injury could guide mobilization of transfusion and hemorrhage-control resources. We developed an arrival-based bedside score and compared its performance with shock index. We studied 239,736 adults with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures in the 2019-2024 National Trauma Data Bank. Major hemorrhage was defined as a hemorrhage-control procedure, hemorrhagic death, or transfusion of ≥ 1000 mL or ≥ 4 units of red blood cells within 4 h. Penalized logistic regression selected arrival variables for an integer score. We assessed performance in a held-out test set (n = 79,912) and at approximately matched alert volume. A model refitted on 2019-2022 admissions was evaluated in 2023-2024. Subgroup analyses were post hoc. Major hemorrhage occurred in 26,479 patients (11.0%); 31.0% were aged ≥ 75 years, and 45.9% had fallen. In the test set, the score achieved an AUROC of 0.882 (95% CI, 0.879-0.886), exceeding shock index by 0.060 (95% CI, 0.055-0.064; P < 0.001). At approximately 15.6% of patients flagged, the score identified 678 additional major hemorrhage cases with 684 fewer false-positive alerts. The temporally validated model achieved an AUROC of 0.885 (95% CI, 0.881-0.888). Discrimination exceeded shock index for pelvic ring disruption (0.830 vs 0.778) and high-energy mechanisms (0.811 vs 0.764), but was lower after falls (0.779 vs 0.800). In patients with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures, an arrival-based score identified major hemorrhage more accurately than shock index at a similar alert burden. Reduced performance after falls and uncertain applicability to suspected fractures warrant caution. External validation and prospective impact assessment are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Does the number of debridement procedures impact risk of infection in open fractures?
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the number of debridements and risk of infection, while stratifying by degree of wound contamination. It was hypothesized that patients with severe contamination, a higher number of debridements would be associated with lower risk of infection. This is a retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected data in the PREP-IT trial (Program of Randomized trials to Evaluate Preoperative antiseptic skin solutions in orthopaedic Trauma). The primary outcome measure was adjudicated surgical site infection. Independent variables were number of debridement procedures and time from injury to definitive wound closure. Analysis was stratified by degree of contamination and multivariable analyses were performed to control for confounders. 3502 total open fractures corresponding to 3222 patients with a median (interquartile range, IQR) age of 42 (29-58) years (2199 [62.8%] men; median (IQR) body mass index 27.7 [24.3-32.6]) were included in this analysis. 2199 patients were included in the non/minimal contamination group, 970 in the surface contamination group, and 333 in the embedded contamination group. After controlling for patient-level characteristics there was a 27% increase in the risk of infection for each debridement performed in the overall patient cohort (OR 1.27 [1.12-1.43] p < 0.001), and a 45% increase in the embedded contamination group (OR, 1.45 [1.12-1.88] p = 0.004). There was no statistically significant difference between minimal contamination groups and the surface contamination group. The results of this study indicate that increased number of debridement procedures was not associated with lower infectious rates. Patients with the highest degree of contamination demonstrated significantly increased risk of developing an infection with each additional debridement. These findings support the importance of limiting unnecessary additional debridement procedures to reduce infection risk and optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack® vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
articles.abstract: SpineJack® vertebral augmentation requires precise bilateral transpedicular access and accurate implant deployment. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and technical performance of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided SpineJack augmentation. This retrospective single-institution, two-site study included consecutive CBCT-guided procedures performed between May 2021 and April 2026. Technical success required planned bilateral implantation, expansion, and cement augmentation without pedicle breach or implant malposition on final CBCT. Secondary outcomes included immediate vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, and treatment setting. The analysis included 178 procedures; median age was 45 years (interquartile range [IQR], 27-59), and 158 procedures (88.8%) involved traumatic fractures. Technical success was 100% (178/178), including 64 procedures (36.0%) with pedicle-implant clearance < 0.8 mm. Median absolute vertebral body height gain was 4.1 mm (IQR, 2.7-6.1), and median restoration of baseline height loss reached 77% (IQR, 47-98). All 24 cement leaks (13.5%) were asymptomatic. No neurological, vascular, infectious, or implant-related complications occurred. Median procedure duration was 60 min (IQR, 50-90), and median dose-area product was 33.2 Gy·cm² (IQR, 19.4-53.1). One hundred procedures (56.2%) were performed on an outpatient basis. CBCT-guided SpineJack augmentation achieved accurate bilateral implant deployment and substantial immediate vertebral height restoration without major procedure-related complications. These findings support CBCT as a reliable guidance strategy for vertebral augmentation, with demonstrated feasibility in outpatient practice.

articles.title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
articles.abstract: Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction. A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System. Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively. MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae. The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

articles.title: Transanal irrigation to treat refractory constipation: a short-term real-life study.
articles.abstract: The treatment of patients complaining of chronic constipation is still far from ideal, and there is a discrete percentage of them that are labeled as refractory to the usual therapeutic approaches. In these patients there is often the need to use alternative approaches. Among these, transanal irrigation seems promising. Our aim was to evaluate the effect of transanal irrigation on symptoms and quality of life in patients with severe refractory constipation. To this end, we retrospectively analyzed the charts of 31 such patients undergoing transanal irrigation, and evaluated them basally and one and three months after the treatment. Data were collected by means of the Wexner score and the SF12 questionnaire for quality of life. Overall, there was a significant decrease of the constipation scores and an improvement of quality of life score after treatment, after both one and three months. No important side effects were documented. In conclusion, treatment with transanal irrigation may be useful, alone or as combination therapy, in patients with constipation refractory to the conventional therapeutic approaches, but studies in more numerous cohorts of subjects are needed to firmly validate this approach.

Topical MSC-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Accelerate Healing of Second-Degree Burns: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn injuries are challenging to treat due to wound progression and long-term scarring. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have regenerative and immunomodulatory properties that may mitigate these complications. In this phase 1/2a, first-in-human, open-label study, a 48-year-old man with deep second-degree burns received a single topical dose of allogeneic bone marrow MSC-derived EVs within 48 h of injury. The treated wound achieved > 99% closure within 1 week, with durable healing for over 1 year. Scar outcomes improved over 52 weeks, with Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale scores indicating early resolution of pain and pruritus and minimal residual scarring. No adverse events occurred. Laser Doppler imaging showed improved perfusion within 1 week, suggesting prevention of burn wound conversion. These findings support the potential of MSC-derived EVs to accelerate burn healing and reduce scar-related morbidity.

articles.title: Reconstruction of the Burned Nose Using an Expanded Skin-Grafted Forehead Flap, Delayed Turnover Flaps, and Indocyanine Green Perfusion Assessment.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Reconstruction of the burned nose is challenging because defects may involve external skin, internal lining, and structural support within scarred or previously grafted tissues. We report the case of a 35-year-old man who sustained an approximately 20% total body surface area flame burn involving the face, neck, chest, and upper extremities, requiring acute excision and split-thickness skin grafting. He later developed a severe postburn nasal deformity with loss of the lower third of the nose, airway compromise, and deficiency of lining, support, and external soft tissue. Both the forehead and nasal dorsum had previously been resurfaced with split-thickness skin grafts, limiting standard reconstructive options. A staged reconstruction was performed using tissue expansion of the grafted forehead, delayed bipedicled turnover flaps from grafted dorsal nasal skin for internal lining, costal cartilage grafting for structural support, and a paramedian forehead flap for external coverage. Intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence angiography was used to assess perfusion and guide operative decision-making. The reconstruction restored nasal contour and airway patency without flap loss, infection, or major complication, and avoided microsurgical free tissue transfer. At long-term follow-up extending to 10 years from the initial injury, the reconstruction remained stable. This case demonstrates that previously grafted tissue can be recruited for complex nasal reconstruction when augmented by tissue expansion, staged delay, and intraoperative perfusion assessment.

articles.title: Pharmacological Management of Atrial Fibrillation Across the Heart Failure Ejection Fraction Spectrum: Rate Control, Rhythm Control, and Beyond.
articles.abstract: To summarise the contemporary pharmacological management of atrial fibrillation (AF) in heart failure (HF), focusing on rate and rhythm control and upstream therapies across the ejection fraction spectrum. Rate control remains a cornerstone of AF management, particularly in permanent AF or haemodynamically fragile patients, with beta-blockers, digoxin, and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers selected according to ejection fraction phenotype. Concurrently, increasing evidence supports early rhythm-control strategies because of their prognostic benefits in HF populations, with current guidelines reinforcing a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-guided approach to antiarrhythmic drug selection. Beyond conventional drugs, HF guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is emerging as an important upstream pharmacological strategy for modulation of the arrhythmogenic substrate. AF management in HF requires an integrated, phenotype-oriented approach combining symptom control, thromboembolic prevention, and optimisation of GDMT. LVEF remains a key determinant of pharmacological safety and therapeutic selection, whereas haemodynamic status primarily guides acute management decisions.

articles.title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF. Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the "female fingerprint" in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: Traumatic hip dislocation: Clinical and epidemiological features, management and prognostic factors in a series of 44 cases from a tertiary centre.
articles.abstract: Traumatic hip dislocation is an uncommon but potentially severe injury requiring emergency management. We aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological features and associated injuries of patients with traumatic hip dislocation treated at a tertiary centre, and to analyse the factors related to complications and to the need for salvage surgery. Retrospective observational study of 44 patients aged 15 years or older treated between 2010 and 2024. Demographic variables, injury mechanism, direction of the dislocation, associated fractures (Judet-Letournel and Pipkin classifications), management and complications were recorded. Bivariate analysis used Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables; a p value < 0.05 was considered significant. Mean age was 37.4 years (SD 19.3) and 70.5% of patients were men. The commonest mechanism was a road traffic accident (52.3%) and the posterior direction was the most frequent (72.7%). A complex dislocation (with an associated fracture) was present in 72.7% of patients, and 36.4% occurred in the context of polytrauma. Closed reduction was performed in 88.6% of cases, with a median time to reduction of 2 h. The most frequent complication was sciatic nerve injury (20.5%). Femoral head osteonecrosis occurred in 2 patients (4.5%). Male sex was associated with more late complications (p = 0.043), and a prolonged hospital stay was associated with both early (p = 0.002) and late (p = 0.017) complications. Complex dislocations showed a consistent trend towards greater morbidity. Traumatic hip dislocation predominantly affects young men after high-energy trauma. Prompt reduction was associated with a low rate of osteonecrosis. The presence of associated fractures and a prolonged hospital stay identify patients with a worse course.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) approach defines safe zones for W-plate fixation of the anterior pelvic ring.
articles.abstract: To define the procedure-specific surgical anatomy of the pre-symphyseal region relevant to W-plate fixation by characterizing the soft-tissue layers, identifying critical neurovascular structures, and defining quantitative safe zones for dissection and plate placement. Fresh-frozen adult cadavers underwent standardized low Pfannenstiel dissections reproducing the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) exposure required for W-plate fixation. Pre-symphyseal soft-tissue layers were sequentially dissected from the skin to the anterior pubic symphysis. The locations of critical neurovascular structures relative to the pubic midline and pubic tubercles were recorded, together with anatomical layers, dimensions of the prepubic ligamentous-aponeurotic complex, soft-tissue thickness, sex-related anatomical differences, and surgical safe zones. Three reproducible anatomical layers were identified in ten specimens. The superficial layer contained the pre-symphyseal fat pad and superficial epigastric vessels. The intermediate layer contained the spermatic cord or round ligament, ilioinguinal and genitofemoral nerves, and suprapubic artery, with these critical structures located at a mean distance of approximately 3.2 cm from the midline. The deep layer was consistently formed by the Pyramidalis-anterior pubic Ligament-Adductor longus Complex (PLAC), which covered the anterior pubic symphysis and measured a mean of 4.6 × 3.1 cm. No critical neurovascular structure crossed the central trajectory corresponding to W-plate placement. Female specimens demonstrated greater preperitoneal soft-tissue thickness, whereas lateral surgical safe zones were narrower in male specimens. The pre-symphyseal region demonstrated a reproducible three-layer surgical anatomy with a predictable distribution of critical neurovascular structures. Quantitative anatomic mapping defined procedure-specific safe zones for extrapelvic W-plate fixation and provided practical guidancefor surgical exposure, implant positioning, and avoidance of iatrogenic injury. Level IV, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Risk factors for complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures carries a substantial risk of postoperative complications, particularly surgical site infection, yet the relative contribution of fracture pattern and associated soft tissue injury to this risk remains incompletely defined. To describe the rate and spectrum of complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures and to identify factors independently associated with these complications, with particular attention to acute surgical site infection. Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 126 patients who underwent surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures between December 2014 and November 2024, reported in accordance with the STROBE statement. Candidate demographic, injury-related, and treatment-related exposures were compared against a composite primary outcome (any postoperative complication) and against acute infection using Fisher's exact test, Pearson chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and multivariable logistic regression. Overall, 39 of 126 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one postoperative complication; chronic pain (22.2%) and acute surgical site infection (16.7%) were the most frequent individual components. In bivariate analysis, the presence of a Morel-Lavallée lesion at baseline was significantly associated with both the composite outcome (OR 12.65, 95% CI 1.42-112.27, p = 0.011) and acute infection (OR 12.12, 95% CI 2.06-71.37, p = 0.007); Young-Burgess fracture pattern was also associated with infection (p = 0.018). After multivariable adjustment for infection, a Morel-Lavallée lesion (adjusted OR 17.69, 95% CI 2.46-126.95, p = 0.004) and combined-mechanism fracture pattern (adjusted OR 8.25 versus anteroposterior compression, 95% CI 1.91-35.58, p = 0.005) remained independently associated with infection. Neither the presence, technique, nor surgical approach of posterior ring fixation was associated with any complication type, and time from injury to definitive fixation (median 13 days) showed no significant association with either outcome. A Morel-Lavallée lesion identified at initial evaluation was associated with postoperative complications in bivariate analysis and, together with a combined-mechanism fracture pattern, remained an independent predictor of surgical site infection after multivariable adjustment. No statistically significant association was identified between posterior fixation technique and complication risk. III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Effects of chronic care model-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This study was conducted to reveal the effects of a Chronic Care Model (CCM)-based intervention offered to elderly patients with diabetes on their medication adherence, self-management, and activities of daily living. This randomized controlled study was conducted on diabetic patients; older adults received inpatient treatment in an internal medicine clinic of a state hospital; the patients in the trial group were provided with training using the CCM. The comparisons following the trial revealed that the differences between the group mean values were statistically significant in all variables except the Katz ADL (p < 0.05). The mean MARS score and mean total DSMS score of the trial group were found to be statistically significantly higher than those of the control group (p < 0.001). The study confirmed that CCM-based interventions offered to elderly patients with diabetes were effective on medication adherence and self-management.

articles.title: [Prolonged mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting].
articles.abstract: Following coronary bypass surgery, postoperative intensive care plays a central role in the subsequent course of the illness. It is well known that patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation have an increased risk of developing numerous secondary organ complications and consequently have higher morbidity and mortality. The objective of this study was to validate established risk factors for prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary bypass surgery in a recent, representative patient collective. In this retrospective, single-center study, all patients who underwent isolated coronary bypass surgery in 2024 and subsequently received interdisciplinary intensive care at the Ulm University Clinic were included. The 312 patients included in the study were between 45 and 85 years old; 84% (n = 262) were male. The median ventilation time for all patients was 15 h (Q1 = 11 h; Q3 = 21 h), whereby 19.5% (n = 61) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). In the multiple logistic regression analysis, intraoperative perfusion time (OR = 1.01; 95% CI 1.0-1.02; p = 0.04) and postoperative peak lactate (OR = 1.26; 95% CI 1.12-1.41; p < 0.001) were significant independent risk factors for PMV. The PMV group also had significantly lower oxygenation indices (Horovitz index = paO2/FiO2), more positive fluid balances on the first and cumulatively on the second postoperative day, longer ischemia and surgical times, and higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) scores. Hospital mortality was significantly higher at 8.2% (n = 5) in the PMV group than in the non-PMV group at 0.8% (n = 2). A comprehensive risk profile for prolonged mechanical ventilation is an essential component of intensive care risk stratification and treatment planning. It enables a differentiated assessment of severity and complexity of underlying diseases and thereby associated organ dysfunction. Against this backdrop, necessary intensive care interventions can be initiated early and potentially contribute to improve treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Lung clearance index and radiological pulmonary involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Lung clearance index (LCI) measures ventilation heterogeneity, but its relationship with pulmonary involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) remains insufficiently characterized. We examined the cross-sectional association of LCI with radiological pulmonary involvement and compared its discrimination with conventional pulmonary function measures, including diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).79 patients with LCH were retrospectively recruited: 54 with and 25 without pulmonary involvement at HRCT). Baseline nitrogen multiple-breath washout, pulmonary function testing, and high-resolution computed tomography were obtained within one week. Analyses included receiver operating characteristic curves, paired DeLong comparisons, and Firth penalized logistic regression. All analyses were exploratory.Mean LCI value in PLCH was significantly higher compared to LCH (mean difference 4.35, 95% CI 3.02-5.67). Its AUC was 0.919 (95% CI 0.861-0.978). In 77 participants with DLCO data, paired AUCs were 0.921 for LCI and 0.751 for DLCO (difference 0.169, 95% CI 0.029-0.309; Holm-adjusted p = 0.018). Higher LCI was associated with radiological pulmonary involvement after adjustment for age, sex and pack-years (adjusted OR per one-unit increase 5.09, 95% CI 2.32-16.67). At the sample-derived threshold > 9.86, sensitivity was 72.2% and specificity 96.0%, with 15 false negatives. Among 42 participants meeting fixed criteria for preserved conventional function, 25 had pulmonary involvement and 14 of these exceeded this threshold.The present study showed higher ventilatory inhomogeneity (higher LCI) in LCH patients with pulmonary involvement compared to LCH ones without it. These exploratory findings support prospective evaluation of LCI as a complementary functional measure. They do not establish early detection, longitudinal prediction, monitoring utility, or safe avoidance of HRCT.

articles.title: Cardiac Autonomic Dysfunction in Diabetic Highlander and Lowlander Populations of Nepal Assessed by Heart Rate Variability.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDiabetes mellitus is associated with cardiac autonomic dysfunction (CAD) and enhanced cardiovascular risk. High-altitude dwellers exhibit physiological adaptations that may regulate autonomic function. The present study aims to compare cardiac autonomic function in diabetic highlanders vs diabetic lowlanders of Nepal using heart rate variability (HRV).MethodsA cross-sectional study was performed on a total of 128 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including 64 native highlanders residing above 2500 m (Phaplu, Solukhumbu district, Nepal) and 64 native lowlanders below 500 m (Biratnagar, Morang District, Nepal). HRV was measured using standard electrocardiography (ECG) under baseline resting state. Time- and frequency-domain HRV indices including age, gender, duration of diabetes, and HbA1c were recorded and analyzed. Comparative statistical analysis was conducted using independent t tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.ResultsIn time-domain HRV parameters, diabetic highlanders showed significantly higher SDNN (88.9 [48.5-97.2] ms vs 28.7 [20.2-43.1] ms; P < .001) and increased RMSSD (64.9 [35.1-92.3] ms vs 21.6 [14.3-38.3] ms; P < .001) compared to lowlanders. Likewise, in frequency-domain HRV analysis, as compared to diabetic lowlanders, diabetic highlanders revealed significantly increased HF power (317.6 [96.5-869.2] ms2 vs 86.1 [29.7-314.0] ms2; P < .001) and lower LF/HF ratio (0.4 [0.2-1.1] vs 1.2 [0.9-3.4]; P < .001) demonstrating relatively better autonomic balance.ConclusionHighlanders with T2DM exhibit relatively preserved cardiac autonomic balance compared to diabetic lowlanders, indicating that chronic exposure to high altitude influences diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction. These findings highlight the importance of considering geographical and environmental factors during management and risk assessment of diabetic individuals in Nepal.

articles.title: Emergency Life-Saving Technician-Performed Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma in Moving Ambulances: A Pilot Innovation Report.
articles.abstract: In Japan, Emergency Life-Saving Technicians (ELSTs) cannot independently perform diagnostic ultrasound under the current legal framework. If ELST-performed focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST) is to be introduced in the prehospital setting, technical feasibility during ambulance motion and the viability of remote physician observation must be established. The study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of ELST-performed FAST in moving ambulances in a controlled manikin setting and to descriptively assess an integrated monitoring system for remote observation. A prospective observational pilot study was conducted at the Okayama City Fire Department Training Center in Okayama Prefecture, Japan on March 3, 2025. Twenty ELSTs completed structured e-learning and a hands-on workshop using standardized FAST/ER FAN manikins. Participants performed FAST under three fixed-order conditions: stationary (STOP), 15km/hour, and 30km/hour on a 250-m circular course. The primary outcome was the total Task-Specific Checklist (TSC) score (0-24 points). Secondary outcomes were examination time, site-specific TSC subscores, inter-rater agreement, and a descriptive assessment of transmitted image quality by two specialist physicians. All 20 ELSTs completed the study. Mean total TSC scores were 23.4 (SD = 0.8) in the STOP condition, 23.4 (SD = 0.9) at 15km/hour, and 23.7 (SD = 0.6) at 30km/hour. Compared with the STOP condition, the mean difference in total TSC score was 0.08 points (95% CI, -0.24 to 0.39; P for noninferiority < 0.001) at 15km/hour and 0.33 points (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.69; P for noninferiority < 0.001) at 30km/hour. Both moving conditions met the pre-specified noninferiority criterion relative to the STOP condition. Mean examination times were 36.7 (SD = 14.4) seconds in the STOP condition, 30.3 (SD = 9.8) seconds at 15km/hour, and 31.9 (SD = 14.8) seconds at 30km/hour. Inter-rater agreement for TSC scoring was moderate (weighted kappa, 0.56). Descriptive ratings suggested that transmitted image quality was generally favorable for remote review in this controlled setting. In this controlled manikin-based pilot study, ELST-performed FAST was technically feasible during moderate ambulance motion, and remote physician observation was feasible. These findings may help inform staged prehospital ultrasound training and future clinical validation under legal and operational constraints.

articles.title: Time to Storm the Next CASTLE: Can Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Improve Outcomes in Patients With Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction?
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation frequently coexist and are linked by shared mechanisms including atrial myopathy, elevated filling pressures, fibrosis, and adverse hemodynamic interactions. The combination of both diseases worsens patient outcomes, and catheter ablation has emerged as a potentially important treatment strategy in this population. This review aims to summarize and highlight the current evidence on ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. When examining outcomes of mortality, hospitalization, hemodynamics, and recurrence, ablation appears to be superior to medical treatment with some mixed results. However, no large trials have been conducted on the topic, and no clear guidelines for ablation in HFpEF patients exist. Ablation is promising but not yet definitive for patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. Ongoing trials, including CASTLE-HFpEF should clarify the gaps including patient selection, procedural strategy, and outcome benefit.
keywords: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

articles.title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
articles.abstract: Patients with acetabular fractures are at significant risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet the optimal chemoprophylactic agent remains undefined. Emerging evidence from elective arthroplasty and general orthopaedic trauma populations suggests that aspirin (ASA) may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ASA compared to other anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention following acetabular fracture surgery. A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a global, web-based health research network that provides on-demand access to de-identified, real-world data from electronic health records and claims. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025 and received VTE prophylaxis within 14 days of surgery were identified. Patients were stratified into ASA (n = 1189) and other anticoagulant (n = 5478) cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, yielding 1174 patients per cohort. Rates and odds of DVT, emergency department (ED) visits, deep infection, stroke, and readmission were assessed at 14-, 30-, and 90-day postoperative intervals. Temporal trends in VTE prophylaxis utilization were also analyzed. Compared to other anticoagulants, ASA was associated with significantly lower odds of DVT at 14 days (1.11% vs. 2.22%; odds ratio [OR]: 0.494; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.253-0.967; P = 0.036), 30 days (1.45% vs. 2.73%; OR: 0.524; 95% CI: 0.290-0.950; P = 0.030), and 90 days (2.56% vs. 4.34%; OR: 0.577; 95% CI: 0.365-0.913; P = 0.018). ASA was also associated with significantly lower odds of ED visits at 90 days (OR: 0.741; 95% CI: 0.570-0.963; P = 0.024). There were no significant differences in deep infection, stroke, or readmission rates. ASA utilization increased from 7.2% in 2014-39.5% in 2025. ASA is safe and effective for DVT prevention following acetabular fracture surgery and is associated with fewer ED visits compared to other anticoagulants. These findings support the growing adoption of ASA as a VTE prophylactic agent in the acetabular fracture population.

articles.title: Common acetabular fracture patterns in patients with femoroacetabular impingement.
articles.abstract: The incidence of acetabular fractures is rising, affecting both younger and elderly patient populations. Developmental abnormalities such as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and hip dysplasia alter hip biomechanics, potentially predisposing younger patients to fracture. FAI, resulting from a cam and/or pincer deformity, is common, affecting 25% of asymptomatic males and 5% of asymptomatic females, and has been linked to hip pain and early osteoarthritis. However, the relationship between FAI morphology and acetabular fracture pattern remains unclear. Patients, 18-55 years old, treated between 2005 and 2023 for acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral head fracture were reviewed for FAI morphology using the Judet and Letournel classification systems. Statistical comparisons were conducted using Fisher's exact tests and unpaired t-tests, with significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 294 patients (72%) exhibited plain radiographic FAI morphology, while 115 (28%) served as controls. The most common fracture pattern in both groups was posterior wall (PW) fractures (23.1% FAI, 31.3% control). Male FAI patients were significantly more likely to experience transverse fractures (p = 0.032, OR=4.6) and posterior column plus PW fractures (p = 0.035, OR=2.5) than controls. Among FAI patients, posterior column fractures were significantly more likely to occur in females (p = 0.011, OR=19). A total of 31 (27.0%) control patients and 63 (21.4%) FAI patients experienced complications. In our data set, FAI patients accounted for 72% of patients undergoing acetabular fracture ORIF. FAI patients most commonly sustained posterior wall fractures, but male FAI patients had a significantly higher rate of transverse and posterior column plus PW. FAI patients experienced a complication rate of 21.4% compared to 27.0% in non-FAI patients.

articles.title: Robotic navigation-assisted versus conventional freehand placement of the infra-acetabular screw in acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract: The infra-acetabular screw (IAS) is an important component of fixation constructs for complex acetabular fractures, but accurate freehand placement is technically demanding, and evidence on robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement remains limited. This study compared robotic navigation-assisted (RA) and conventional fluoroscopic freehand (CF) IAS placement in acetabular fracture surgery. In this retrospective study, 53 patients with acetabular fractures who underwent IAS fixation between June 2022 and July 2024 were included, 28 underwent RA placement using the HoloSight robotic navigation system and 25 underwent CF placement. The primary outcome was screw-placement accuracy, graded on postoperative CT according to the Lonstein criteria. Secondary outcomes included the number of guide-wire adjustments, fluoroscopy frequency, IAS insertion time, total operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture reduction quality, hip function, and complications. The grade 0 (no cortical penetration) rate was higher in the RA group than in the CF group (96.4% [27/28] vs. 60.0% [15/25], p = 0.005). RA placement was associated with fewer guide-wire adjustments (0.07 ± 0.26 vs. 3.60 ± 1.15), fewer fluoroscopies (9.32 ± 1.66 vs. 21.28 ± 3.18), shorter IAS insertion time (10.36 ± 2.50 vs. 26.68 ± 4.11 min), shorter total operative time (134.54 ± 15.46 vs. 155.80 ± 18.48 min), and less intraoperative blood loss (468.21 ± 84.68 vs. 588.40 ± 80.76 mL) (all p < 0.001). The mean follow-up duration was 15.7 ± 2.0 months (range, 13-22 months). Reduction quality, hip function, and complication rates did not differ significantly between the two groups. Robotic navigation-assisted IAS placement was associated with significantly higher screw-placement accuracy and greater procedural efficiency than the conventional freehand technique, without compromising fracture reduction quality, hip function, or safety.

articles.title: The prevalence of mental health service use after long-term minor-to-moderate motor vehicle crash injury: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Minor to moderate motor vehicle crash (MVC) injuries can lead to persistent psychological distress, yet evidence regarding mental health service (MHS) use is limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and characterise the determinants of MHS use after minor to moderate MVC injury. This retrospective cohort study examined Australians with work-related, MVC injuries and workers' compensation claims exceeding 24 months duration. Claims and services data were linked with healthcare records to capture MHS use before and after injury. The injured group was divided into severity sub-groups based on hospital admission status (hospitalised, non-hospitalised). A community comparator group was matched to the non-hospitalised group based on gender and injury year. The primary outcome was MHS period prevalence within 24 months. Determinants of MHS were identified through binomial logistic regression. There were 574 non-hospitalised, 293 hospitalised, and 8294 community comparators included in the study cohort. The prevalence of MHS use at 24 months post injury was highest for the hospitalised group (36.9%), followed by the non-hospitalised group (31.5%) and community comparators (13.5%). The non-hospitalised group had 3.14 times greater odds (95% CI 2.53, 3.88) of MHS use compared to community comparators, and had the highest prevalence of publicly-funded MHS (18.8%). Hospitalised participants (28.3%) had a higher prevalence of workers' compensation funded MHS compared to non-hospitalised participants (19.3%). The adjusted odds of MHS use were higher among females (OR 2.05 [1.42, 2.97]), and people who had used MHS in the 12 months prior to injury (OR 4.66 [2.41, 9.50]). People with non-hospitalised MVC injuries had a significantly higher prevalence of MHS use compared with their matched community comparator group, and people with hospitalised MVC injuries had the highest prevalence at 24 months-follow up. The highest proportion of people assessing publicly funded MHS was by people in the non-hospitalised group. These findings highlight the ongoing mental health needs of people with minor to moderate MVC injury. Monitoring for the early post injury psychological signs and symptoms, and timely referral to MHS, could reduce psychological burden following MVC injury.

articles.title: Is surgeon technique a modifiable risk factor for heterotopic ossification after posterior acetabular fracture fixation? A multi-surgeon study.
articles.abstract: Heterotopic ossification (HO) is a well-recognized complication following operative fixation of acetabular fractures through a posterior approach. Established risk factors largely reflect nonmodifiable patient and injury characteristics. Whether surgeon-controlled aspects of operative technique influence HO remains poorly defined. The purpose of this study was to determine if the individual surgeon and specific technique variables are associated with HO after accounting for established patient and injury factors. We retrospectively reviewed 1292 patients who underwent acetabular fracture fixation through a Kocher-Langenbeck approach at two Level 1 trauma centers between 2010 and 2025 by 14 fellowship-trained orthopaedic traumatologists. Patients receiving any form of HO prophylaxis were excluded. Four surgeon-controlled variables were examined: aggressiveness of gluteus minimus debridement, trochanteric osteotomy, thrombin gel use, and closed suction drainage. HO was graded on final radiographs by two independent reviewers using the Brooker classification, with third-reader adjudication for disagreements, and categorized as little-to-no (grade 0-I), moderate (grade II), or severe (grade III-IV). Mixed-effects logistic regression models with surgeon as a random effect were used to assess the associations between patient, injury, and surgeon-controlled technique variables, as well as the individual surgeon, with severe and moderate HO formation. Little-to-no HO occurred in 1132 patients (87.6%), moderate HO in 96 (7.4%), and severe HO in 64 (5.0%). Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement was not associated with HO severity. For severe HO, the surgeon did not contribute meaningfully to model performance, and no surgeon-controlled technique variables were significant; severe head injury, mechanical ventilation beyond 72 h, African-American race, and dual surgical approaches were associated with severe HO. For moderate HO, the surgeon contributed moderately, and both trochanteric osteotomy (odds ratio [OR] 3.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-12) and closed suction drainage (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.0-3.1) were associated with increased odds of moderate HO. Severe HO following posterior acetabular fracture fixation is predominantly driven by patient and injury characteristics rather than surgeon technique. Aggressive gluteus minimus debridement does not appear to reduce HO risk, and prevention efforts should prioritize patient-level risk stratification.

articles.title: Influencing factors of the long-term predictive accuracy of the ocular trauma score.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the performance of the Ocular Trauma Score (OTS) in predicting long-term visual outcomes after mechanical ocular trauma and to identify the key factors influencing its accuracy. This retrospective study enrolled 106 patients with mechanical ocular trauma, with a median follow-up of 14 months. Retrieved variables included demographic characteristics and clinical data after the injury. The distribution of final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was compared between the actual outcomes and the OTS-predicted outcomes. A weighted average predicted BCVA was calculated based on the BCVA probability distribution for each OTS category to classify patients into Better (actual BCVA better than OTS predicted) and Non-Better groups. Factors associated with OTS prediction discrepancies were identified using univariate analyses. Multivariable Firth logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation was performed to identify factors independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes. The OTS demonstrated a clear severity-dependent predictive pattern. Predictive accuracy was highest for mild injuries (OTS category 5) but showed a systematic pessimistic bias in severe injuries (OTS category 1), overestimating poor outcomes (NLP) and underestimating recovery potential (BCVA grades 3-5). For intermediate injuries (OTS categories 2-3), the likelihood of achieving moderate vision (20/200-20/50) was underestimated. Multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis (p = 0.021). In the multivariable analysis, endophthalmitis (odds ratio [OR] = 2.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-8.29, p = 0.034) and penetrating injury (OR = 3.71, 95% CI: 1.17-12.94, p = 0.026) were independently associated with better-than-predicted outcomes, whereas initial BCVA grade 2, despite a significant univariate association, did not retain statistical significance after adjustment (OR = 2.01, 95% CI: 0.79-5.10, p = 0.144). The OTS remains a useful prognostic tool but demonstrates limited accuracy in severe mechanical ocular trauma. Endophthalmitis and penetrating injury were identified as independent modifiers, while initial BCVA grade 2 and multiple surgeries were associated with better-than-predicted outcomes in the univariate analysis. Contextualising its predictions with contemporary surgical factors and clinical modifiers may improve the individualised application of the OTS.

articles.title: Personality Traits and Professional Quality of Life in Volunteer Ski Patrollers.
articles.abstract: IntroductionSki patrollers, as outdoor emergency first responders, face unique occupational trauma exposure that impacts their professional quality of life. Despite these exposures, this population has been largely understudied in trauma research. Personality traits have been associated with outcomes from occupational trauma exposure in other populations. This study investigates associations between personality traits and outcomes including compassion fatigue and satisfaction in volunteer ski patrollers.MethodsVolunteers from a ski patrol in the Pacific Northwest (n = 82) completed a cross-sectional online survey measuring trauma exposure, the 5-factor model personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion, agreeableness, openness, and conscientiousness), and professional quality of life variables of compassion fatigue (comprising burnout and secondary traumatic stress [STS]) and compassion satisfaction.ResultsThose who reported trauma exposure while patrolling endorsed higher compassion satisfaction and lower burnout. Extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness correlated negatively with burnout and positively with compassion satisfaction. Extraversion and conscientiousness negatively correlated with STS, while neuroticism positively correlated with burnout and STS but negatively correlated with compassion satisfaction.ConclusionsOur findings highlight the association between personality traits and professional quality of life outcomes. Organizations could use this data to design tailored interventions to support ski patrollers in managing occupational trauma exposure. Individuals high in neuroticism endorsed more negative outcomes and could potentially benefit most from preventative measures and intervention compared to those high in extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness.

articles.title: No Woman Left Un-Kitted: Is the Traditional Expedition Medical Kit Really Fit for Women?
Unplanned return to hospital from hospital-at-home care: incidence, timing, and determinants.
articles.abstract: Unplanned transfer from Hospital-at-Home (HaH) to conventional inpatient care-termed clinical escalation-is widely used as a safety indicator, yet its incidence, timing, and physiological patterns across heterogeneous HaH populations remain poorly characterised. Retrospective cohort study of consecutive HaH episodes from January 2021 to December 2025 was performed at a tertiary academic centre. Clinical escalation was defined as unplanned transfer from HaH requiring ≥ 24 h of inpatient care due to clinical deterioration or acute intercurrent illness, and was manually adjudicated (κ = 0.90). Physiological triggers were classified into predefined domains. Severe escalation was defined as ICU admission or in-hospital death. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with escalation. Amongst 10,167 episodes (mean age 70.9 years; 44.0% women), clinical escalation occurred in 508 (5.0%; 95% CI 4.6-5.4). Median time to escalation was 6 days (IQR 3-12); only 24.6% of events occurred within 72 h. Respiratory (30.5%) and infectious (18.1%) deterioration were the most frequent triggers. Severe escalation occurred in 169 episodes (33.3%). Higher age-adjusted Charlson index (OR per point 1.11; 95% CI 1.06-1.15) and early-discharge admission from hospital wards (OR 1.69; 95% CI 1.25-2.28 vs. direct home admission) were independently associated with escalation. Model discrimination was modest (AUC 0.68). Clinical escalation in HaH affected approximately 1 in 20 episodes and followed identifiable temporal and physiological patterns. Risk was shaped by comorbidity burden and care trajectory rather than static admission characteristics. These findings support interpreting escalation as an expected and clinically interpretable component of acute home-based care rather than solely as a marker of programme failure.

articles.title: Initial Emergency Department Concentrations of Serum Bicarbonate and Lactate Are Associated With Survival to Hospital Discharge in Children Following Submersion Injuries.
articles.abstract: There is a lack of objective measures to determine outcome and disposition following pediatric submersion injury.
